sections.h2: How do I sell my house fast in Duluth, GA?
sections.html:
In Duluth you can list the house, sell it yourself, or take a cash offer that buys the home as-is and closes on your date. The right pick depends on repairs, tenants, liens and how soon you need to move.

Duluth is a Gwinnett County city that has kept growing. The Census Bureau estimates 33,815 residents as of July 1, 2025, compared with 31,873 in the April 2020 Census and 26,600 in 2010. About 56.5% of homes are owner-occupied, so owners here sell alongside a sizable renter population, and many local sellers are investors, heirs or people relocating for work.

A fast sale makes the most sense when the house needs a roof, kitchen or foundation work you would rather not fund, when you are carrying two mortgages, or when an estate has to be settled.

sections.h2: What does the Census say about Duluth households and housing costs?
sections.html:
For 2020 to 2024, the median value of owner-occupied homes in Duluth is $400,800 and median household income is $95,331. Median monthly owner costs are $2,116 with a mortgage and $678 without. Median gross rent is $1,828.

The city has a large immigrant community: 30.9% of residents are foreign-born and 38.3% of people age 5 and over speak a language other than English at home. For a seller, that means buyers and tenants come from many backgrounds, and listings or flyers in more than one language can widen interest.

sections.h2: Where did Duluth get its name, and how did the town develop?
sections.html:
Duluth sits on land that was Cherokee territory until Gwinnett County was created in 1818. The city's history page says Evan Howell settled the area in 1821, and the crossroads he built became known as Howell's Cross Roads for about 40 years.

The railroad reached the town in 1871, and the name changed to Duluth in 1873 after Congress took up a bill about a railroad to Duluth, Minnesota. The state approved an official charter in 1876, and the city was formally incorporated in 1906. Duluth also elected Georgia's first female mayor, Alice Harrell Strickland, in 1922.

The city's seal still carries a steam engine and cotton, and a plan to restore the historic downtown was approved in 1998. For sellers, the old downtown core and the newer commercial corridor along Interstate 85 and Buford Highway are two different buyer pitches: walkable character in one, quick highway access in the other.

sections.h2: Which roads and areas should I mention to Duluth buyers?
sections.html:
Duluth's own materials name Interstate 85, Buford Highway, Peachtree Industrial Boulevard, Georgia Highway 120 and Pleasant Hill Road as its main transportation routes. The city describes itself as about 25 miles northeast of Atlanta. The Census puts mean travel time to work at 29.9 minutes.

Highlight the features that match those routes:

  • Distance to Interstate 85 and the Pleasant Hill Road corridor for commuters.
  • Closeness to downtown events and the Southeastern Railway Museum for buyers who like a town-center setting.
  • Nearby parks and green space, since the city has been a designated Tree City since 1989 according to its history page.
  • Proximity to shopping and dining along the commercial corridors.

Be accurate about distances and school assignment, and let buyers confirm both for the exact address rather than quoting a boundary from memory.

sections.h2: Does Duluth charge its own property tax, and how does it work at closing?
sections.html:
Yes. The City of Duluth bills, collects and disburses its own property tax, separate from the Gwinnett County bill. The city uses values set by the Gwinnett County Tax Assessor's Office and a millage rate adopted by the City Council.

For tax year 2026 the city's page says notices were mailed at the end of September and are due by December 15, 2026, with any unpaid prior-year amounts added to the 2026 bill. The city also adds an annual stormwater fee to the bill: for 2026 it is $92.70 for most detached single-family homes and $46.35 for most condominiums and townhomes.

If you are a new owner who has not received a city bill by October 15, the city asks you to email or call its property tax office. When you sell, ask the closing attorney to check both the city bill and the Gwinnett County bill, since each is paid separately.

sections.h2: How do Gwinnett homestead exemptions affect a Duluth sale?
sections.html:
The Gwinnett County Tax Commissioner handles homestead applications for Duluth owners, using one application for all of its exemptions. You must own and occupy the property as your primary residence on January 1, or an approved application applies to the following year.

Applications are accepted year-round, but you need to apply by the appeal deadline printed on your Notice of Assessment for the exemption to count for the current year. The county asks for 6 to 8 weeks to review a request. Exemptions renew automatically unless something changes.

Changes that call for a new application include turning 62 or older, a new disability or veteran status, a name change, and moving the deed into a trust. A person who buys your house applies on their own after the closing, so do not expect your exemption to carry over.

sections.h2: What local rules should I check before selling a Duluth house?
sections.html:
Duluth's Planning and Development department handles permits, inspections, land use applications and ordinances, and the city's code of ordinances is posted online. If you have an unfinished addition, a deck built without a permit, or a pending stormwater issue, contact that department before a buyer's inspector raises it.

The city's Zoning Board of Appeals and Planning Commission pages are useful if you want to know whether a variance or rezoning is under discussion near your lot. Duluth also runs a city clerk office that handles occupational tax and business applications, which matters if you operate a business from the house.

When the buyer is a cash purchaser, these items still come up in the title review, so tell the buyer what you know about open permits, unpaid fees and violations up front.

sections.h2: Should I take a cash offer or list my Duluth house?
sections.html:
Take a cash offer when speed and certainty matter more to you than the last dollar of price. List the house when it is in good condition and you can wait for showings, an inspection and a buyer's loan approval.

Ask any cash buyer for terms in writing: the price, who pays closing costs, the closing date, and what happens if the buyer does not close. Then ask what you would net after your mortgage payoff, the city and county tax bills, and any liens. A written net figure lets you compare it with a listing on fair terms.

If the house is part of an estate or has several owners, settle who has the authority to sign before you start, since that is the most common cause of delay.

faqs.q: When is the City of Duluth property tax bill due?
faqs.a: For tax year 2026 the city set a December 15, 2026 due date, with notices mailed at the end of September. Check the city's property tax page each year, because the dates are published annually.

faqs.q: Do I pay both city and county property tax on a Duluth house?
faqs.a: Yes. The City of Duluth bills its own property tax, and Gwinnett County bills separately. The city uses values from the Gwinnett County Tax Assessor and a millage rate set by the City Council.

faqs.q: What is the stormwater fee on a Duluth tax bill?
faqs.a: The city's page lists $92.70 for 2026 for most detached single-family homes and $46.35 for most condominiums and townhomes. The fee appears on the property tax bill.

faqs.q: How long does a Gwinnett homestead application take to review?
faqs.a: The county asks owners to allow 6 to 8 weeks. Applications are accepted year-round, with the appeal deadline on your Notice of Assessment controlling the current year.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Duluth?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau lists $400,800 as the median value of owner-occupied homes in Duluth for 2020 to 2024. A specific house can be priced above or below that figure.
